title: Connection Between a Restaurant and a Delivery Location
real_world_story: The platform needs to know whether a rider can travel from a restaurant to a delivery location through any sequence of roads. The delivery region is modeled as a directed graph. Use a depth-first traversal to determine whether the delivery location is reachable from the restaurant.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following roads as far as possible to discover whether the delivery is possible

problem_statement: Given a directed graph with N nodes and M edges, and two nodes S and T, determine whether there is a path from S to T. Print YES if T is reachable from S, otherwise print NO.
task: Use DFS to check whether the delivery location is reachable from the restaurant.
input_format: The first line contains four integers N, M, S and T, where N is the number of nodes (numbered 1 to N), M is the number of directed edges, S is the restaurant, and T is the delivery location. The next M lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a directed road from node U to node V.
output_format: Print YES if node T is reachable from node S, otherwise print NO.

examples.explanation: The rider can follow 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 (and also 1 -> 2 -> 4) to reach the delivery location.
There is no road leading from node 1 toward node 4, so the delivery location is unreachable.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS explores one connected route as far as possible and can determine whether the target is reachable using recursion or an explicit stack.

hint: Begin the traversal at the restaurant node S.
Visit a neighbor and follow it as far as possible before backtracking.
If the delivery location T is visited, it is reachable.
real_world_takeaway: DFS helps a delivery platform quickly confirm whether an order can even be served, avoiding dispatch attempts for impossible routes.
